minutes.headline: Commission approved a garage at 22 Fairview Rd, lifted the cease-and-desist at 7-Eleven Mass Ave, and continued 390 Howard St.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard a Parks update on town beach sand work, approved one notice of intent, and continued several hearings to January. The longest discussion was the 390 Howard Street delineation, where members asked for flags on permanent stakes, an updated plan and a redelineation. They also discussed the legal-ad payment problem with the Ledger, and lifted the cease-and-desist at 7-Eleven Mass Ave.

public_comment.topic: Chair invited public comment at the start; no hands raised.
Chair invited public comment on 22 Fairview Road; none offered.
Suggested the commission follow other towns' practice of having the applicant pay the paper for legal ads directly, and no payment means no hearing.

budget_items.what_was_said: Applicants have for over a year been asked to pay The Lunenburg Ledger directly instead of paying the town. This was changed because ads were paid from the land use office budget, which ran short in busy years.
Matt Morrow said applicants previously wrote the town a check for each legal ad, deposited to the general fund, and transfers to the advertising budget were needed in busy years.
A commitment letter vote was no longer needed; the grant was already written and GIS time belongs to the planning board.

budget_items.topic: Removal of shed/barn at 950 Chase Ave conservation land
budget_items.what_was_said: The facilities manager obtained an informal estimate for removal and demolition; the commission will return to the town manager and counsel on next steps.
The town paid membership for active members, and a commissioner donated for the handbook.

decisions.decision: Members asked the applicant at 390 Howard St to have engineers survey-locate the 2008 flags on permanent stakes, redelineate wetlands under current conditions, and update the plan to show site work.
Matt Morrow will work with the office to schedule a site inspection and check flags beforehand; the hearing was continued to January 17 rather than January 3.
Sophie will call The Ledger to learn the root cause of the legal ad problem and ask about an online payment process like Gardner's.
The Trails Vision Grant item was converted to an FYI: Bob put the town in for the grant and Heather wrote the letter.
Chair will seek public volunteers for an Earth Day 2024 work group; no objections raised.
Target of March set for finishing the web presence cleanup and QR-code brochure.
No member volunteered for the stormwater task force seat; deferred.
Enforcement order at 7-Eleven stays active until planting is done, though work can continue.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted 5-0 to approve a notice of intent for a garage addition at 22 Fairview Road with standard conditions.
The 390 Howard Street delineation hearing was continued to January 17, 2024, after members asked for flags on permanent stakes, a redelineation and an updated plan.
Members voted to lift the cease-and-desist at 7-Eleven Mass Ave so drainage can be installed; the enforcement order stays active until planting is done.
Hearings at 255 Sunny Hill Road and 20 Kilber Street lots 1-3 were each continued to January 3, and 171 Arbor Street was continued at the applicant's request.
Staff will call The Ledger to learn why legal-ad payment broke down, and ask about an online payment process.

why_it_matters: Who pays for legal ads on wetlands hearings, the applicant directly or the town, affects the land use office budget and whether a hearing can proceed.
The continued hearings, including 390 Howard Street and 7-Eleven Mass Ave, decide what neighbors and abutters can build or must restore near wetlands in the new year.
watch_next: January 3, 2024: continued hearings at 255 Sunny Hill Road and 20 Kilber Street lots 1-3.
January 17, 2024: continued 390 Howard Street delineation hearing, after a site inspection and flag check.
